comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. GitHub #642's second design (mitcad#2415; opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/shell-sharp-reported-test.cmake): Body2 (F7.b0), a disk (Extrude2 F7, radius 33, z 50..90) with an arm (Extrude3 F8, z 60..80) whose flat sides are tangent to it, a boss on the arm's round end (Extrude4 F9) and the disk's rims rounded 3 mm (Fillet1 F10). The disk's seam lies on one of the arm's tangent lines. The saved Shell2 (F18, the timeline marker right after it) is Rounded; the report's picture: Inside 2 mm, Sharp, Tangent Chain off, the boss top removed. Sharp failed ('the offset faces do not close up') at any thickness: the geometry kernel's offset took the tangent edge on the seam's line for a seam and left its offset untrimmed, and the arm's side on the seam got no inside (OCCT port patch 2415).
Both arm sides, the disk's side and the arm's round end with the inside of their wall, 2 mm in.
The volume of the wall: the geometry kernel's 43304.5 mm3 in the OCCT lab, as the same body with the disk's seam turned off the tangent line gives (Rounded 43121.6).
1 mm: 22287.4 mm3 (the same with the seam turned away).

5 mm (mitcad#2464, the reporter's follow-up on 0.73.0, which refused with 'nothing can be hollowed' under 11 faces): the wall thicker than the disk's 3 mm rims, whose roundings vanish in the offset (the insides of the faces beside them meet, OCCT port patch 0100). The geometry kernel's thick solid of the same body rebuilt in the OCCT lab (geometry.shell_seam_on_tangent_edge's body, whose 1 and 2 mm volumes are these): 98489.8 mm3, the seam on the tangent line or at +x alike.
The rims' roundings have no inside of the wall: the feature says so in a note.
